scenario: 视频推荐要在总延迟 <200ms 内，从数百万视频里选出并排好一屏推荐。
scenario_en: Video recommendation must select and order a screen of recommendations from millions of videos within <200ms total latency.
q: 在线服务的两阶段流水线由哪几段组成，各自的量级延迟是多少？
q_en: What stages make up the two-stage serving pipeline, and roughly how much latency does each take?
why: 三段：候选生成(~20ms，ANN 召回~500个)→排序(~50ms，W&D/DCN 精排)→重排(~10ms，多样性+硬过滤)。核心计算约 80ms，留余量给网络/特征拉取，凑成 <200ms 预算。
why_en: Three stages: candidate generation (~20ms, ANN pulls ~500), ranking (~50ms, Wide&Deep/DCN), re-ranking (~10ms, diversity + hard filters), about 80ms of core compute inside the <200ms budget.
diagram:
flowchart LR U["用户请求"] --> C["候选生成
~20ms · ANN→~500"] C --> R["排序
~50ms · W&D/DCN"] R --> RR["重排
~10ms · 多样性+过滤"] RR --> F["返回一屏"]
options: 单阶段：一个大模型直接对数百万视频逐个实时打分并排序
两阶段：先用精排模型算全量、再做召回粗筛，最后不做重排
候选生成~20ms→排序~50ms→重排~10ms
召回→排序→召回→排序 反复迭代直到收敛，不设任何延迟预算
options_en: Single stage: one big model scores and orders all millions of videos in real time.
Two stages: rank the full corpus with the heavy model first, then coarse-retrieve, with no re-ranking.
Candidate generation ~20ms → ranking ~50ms → re-ranking ~10ms.
Retrieve → rank → retrieve → rank repeatedly until convergence, with no latency budget at all.
optionExplanations: 对数百万逐个跑重模型远超 200ms，正是两阶段漏斗要避免的；必须先召回缩小候选。
顺序反了：先召回粗筛把数百万压到几百，再排序精算；且生产系统一定有重排。
对；漏斗把重计算限制在几百候选上，各段延迟相加还留出网络/特征的余量。
反复迭代无界会爆延迟；在线服务是单向漏斗且有硬延迟预算。
optionExplanations_en: Running a heavy model over millions blows past 200ms—exactly what the two-stage funnel avoids; retrieve first to shrink candidates.
Order is reversed: retrieval coarse-filters millions to hundreds first, then ranking; production always has re-ranking.
Correct — the funnel confines heavy compute to a few hundred candidates, and the summed stage latencies leave headroom for network/features.
Unbounded iteration explodes latency; online serving is a one-way funnel with a hard latency budget.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务第一阶段，用 ANN 从数百万里召回约 500 个候选，追求召回和吞吐。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Candidate generation is stage one: ANN pulls ~500 candidates from millions, optimizing recall and throughput.

scenario: 要评估候选生成阶段本身好不好，而不是评估最终排序。
scenario_en: You need to evaluate the candidate-generation stage itself, not the final ordering.
q: Recall@K 衡量的是什么？
q_en: What does Recall@K measure?
why: Recall@K = 从数百万里检索出的 top-K 中，真正相关视频所占的比例。它只看「有没有被召回进 top-K」，不看排序顺序，是候选生成阶段的核心指标。
why_en: Recall@K is the fraction of truly relevant videos captured in the top-K retrieved from millions; it measures coverage, not ordering, and is the candidate-generation metric.
options: top-K 检索结果中真正相关视频的比例
把相关视频排在越靠前得分越高的位置加权质量
用户看完一个视频后的平均观看时长与完播率
模型推理一次的平均端到端延迟毫秒数
options_en: The share of truly relevant videos inside the top-K retrieved.
A position-weighted quality that scores relevant videos higher when ranked earlier.
The average watch time and completion rate after a user finishes a video.
The average end-to-end latency in milliseconds of one model inference.
optionExplanations: 对；Recall@K 只问「相关的有没有进 top-K」，是覆盖率指标，忽略顺序。
位置加权是 NDCG@K 的定义，不是 Recall@K；Recall 不看顺序。
观看时长是在线参与度指标，不是离线召回覆盖率。
延迟是服务性能指标，和召回覆盖率无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — Recall@K only asks whether the relevant items made the top-K; it is a coverage metric ignoring order.
Position weighting defines NDCG@K, not Recall@K; recall ignores order.
Watch time is an online engagement metric, not offline retrieval coverage.
Latency is a serving-performance metric, unrelated to retrieval coverage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检索出的前 K 个里，真正相关物料所占的比例，衡量召回覆盖率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recall@K is the fraction of truly relevant items among the top-K retrieved, measuring retrieval coverage.

scenario: 候选生成的 Recall@K 很低，很多真正相关的视频根本没进召回结果。
scenario_en: Candidate generation has low Recall@K—many truly relevant videos never make it into the retrieved set.
q: 低 Recall@K 会对整条流水线产生什么后果？
q_en: What does a low Recall@K do to the whole pipeline?
why: 召回是漏斗上游：没被召回的视频，排序永远看不到，也就没机会被推。低 Recall@K 会「饿死」整条流水线，再强的排序也救不回漏掉的候选。
why_en: Retrieval is the funnel's top: videos not retrieved are never seen by the ranker, so low Recall@K starves the whole pipeline, and no ranker can recover missed candidates.
options: 没影响，排序模型会自动把漏掉的相关视频补回来
排序永远看不到漏掉的候选，整条流水线被饿死
只会略微增加端到端延迟，推荐质量基本不变
会提高多样性，因为候选更少、分布更集中
options_en: No impact, the ranker automatically pulls back the relevant videos that were missed.
The ranker never sees the missed candidates, so the whole pipeline starves.
It only slightly increases end-to-end latency, with recommendation quality basically unchanged.
It improves diversity because there are fewer, more concentrated candidates.
optionExplanations: 排序只能给召回给它的东西排序，看不到没召回的，补不回来。
对；这是漏斗的硬约束——上游漏了，下游无从弥补，Recall@K 决定天花板。
问题不是延迟而是覆盖率：好内容根本没进候选，质量直接受损。
漏掉相关视频不是多样性，是覆盖缺口，会降低相关性而非提升多样性。
optionExplanations_en: The ranker can only order what retrieval hands it; it cannot see or recover what was never retrieved.
Correct — this is the funnel's hard constraint: what the top misses, downstream cannot fix; Recall@K sets the ceiling.
The issue is coverage, not latency: good content never entered candidates, directly hurting quality.
Missing relevant videos is a coverage gap, not diversity; it lowers relevance rather than raising diversity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 上游召回漏掉的候选，下游排序永远拿不到，质量被上游封顶。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pipeline starvation is when candidates missed by upstream retrieval never reach downstream ranking, capping quality.

scenario: 要评估排序阶段的好坏，且第 1 位的相关视频应该比第 10 位的更值钱。
scenario_en: You need to evaluate the ranking stage, where a relevant video at position 1 should count far more than at position 10.
q: NDCG@K 相比 Recall@K 多考虑了什么？
q_en: What does NDCG@K account for that Recall@K does not?
why: NDCG@K 是位置加权的相关性：排在前面的相关视频得分远高于排在后面的，模拟用户注意力随位置衰减。Recall@K 只看在不在 top-K，不看顺序。
why_en: NDCG@K is position-weighted relevance—a relevant video ranked earlier scores far higher, mirroring attention decay—whereas Recall@K ignores order.
options: 只看相关视频有没有进 top-K，完全忽略先后顺序
衡量模型推理延迟随排名位置的变化
统计用户对每个位置视频的绝对打星数
位置加权的相关性：越靠前得分越高
options_en: Only whether relevant videos made it into the top-K, ignoring order entirely.
How inference latency changes with rank position.
Users’ absolute star ratings for the video at each position.
Position-weighted relevance: the earlier a relevant video sits, the higher it scores.
optionExplanations: 只看在不在 top-K 是 Recall@K；NDCG 的关键增量正是位置权重。
延迟是服务指标，NDCG 是排序质量指标，不相关。
NDCG 用的是隐式反馈标签，不是绝对打星；且它按位置加权而非计星。
对；位置折扣是 NDCG 的核心，让「把相关的排前面」得到奖励。
optionExplanations_en: Whether items are in the top-K is Recall@K; NDCG's added value is exactly the position weighting.
Latency is a serving metric; NDCG is a ranking-quality metric, unrelated.
NDCG uses implicit-feedback labels, not absolute stars, and weights by position rather than counting stars.
Correct — the position discount is NDCG's core, rewarding putting relevant items earlier.

termDefinitions.fullName: Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain at K
termDefinitions.meaning: 位置加权的排序质量指标，越靠前的相关结果贡献越大，再对理想排序归一化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG@K (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain at K) is a position-weighted ranking metric where earlier relevant results contribute more, normalized to the ideal order.

scenario: 离线评估要同时衡量「召回够不够全」和「排得好不好」，需要两个不同指标。
scenario_en: Offline evaluation must measure both 'did retrieval cover enough' and 'is the order good', needing two different metrics.
q: Recall@K 和 NDCG@K 分别评估哪个阶段、有何互补？
q_en: Which stage does each of Recall@K and NDCG@K evaluate, and how are they complementary?
why: Recall@K 评候选生成，只看覆盖率、不看顺序；NDCG@K 评排序，位置加权看顺序质量。前者定天花板、后者定天花板内的排列质量，两者互补。
why_en: Recall@K evaluates candidate generation (coverage, order-agnostic); NDCG@K evaluates ranking (position-weighted order quality)—one sets the ceiling, the other the ordering quality within it.
tradeoff: Recall@K 管覆盖(不看序) vs NDCG@K 管排序质量(看序)
options: 两者都评排序阶段，只是 K 的取值不同而已
Recall@K 评排序阶段、NDCG@K 评候选生成阶段
Recall@K 评候选生成看覆盖率，NDCG@K 评排序看顺序
两者都评候选生成阶段，NDCG@K 只是 Recall@K 的归一化版本
options_en: Both evaluate the ranking stage and differ only in the value of K.
Recall@K evaluates the ranking stage and NDCG@K evaluates candidate generation.
Recall@K evaluates candidate generation for coverage; NDCG@K evaluates ranking for ordering quality.
Both evaluate candidate generation, and NDCG@K is just a normalized version of Recall@K.
optionExplanations: 两者评的是不同阶段(召回 vs 排序)，不是同指标换 K。
说反了：Recall 管召回覆盖、NDCG 管排序顺序。
对；覆盖率定上限，位置加权质量定上限内的好坏，正好互补。
NDCG 不是 Recall 的归一化；它引入位置折扣、评的是排序阶段。
optionExplanations_en: They evaluate different stages (retrieval vs ranking), not the same metric with a different K.
Backwards: Recall covers retrieval coverage, NDCG covers ranking order.
Correct — coverage sets the ceiling and position-weighted quality sets the goodness within it, complementary.
NDCG is not a normalized Recall; it introduces a position discount and evaluates the ranking stage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用历史数据(不上线)衡量模型质量，如 Recall@K、NDCG@K。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Offline evaluation measures model quality on historical data without deploying, e.g. Recall@K, NDCG@K.

scenario: 要为 NDCG@K 构造 ground-truth 相关性标签，但用户几乎不会显式打星，且打星样本极少。
scenario_en: You must build ground-truth relevance labels for NDCG@K, but users rarely give explicit star ratings and such samples are scarce.
q: 相关性标签该用显式打星还是隐式反馈来构造？
q_en: Should relevance labels come from explicit stars or implicit feedback?
why: 用隐式反馈(观看时长分桶、点赞、转发)构造标签：显式打星稀疏、有偏、大多数用户不打。隐式信号量大、覆盖全，但要小心它也带偏差(如标题党骗点)。标签构造本身就是设计决策。
why_en: Build labels from implicit feedback (watch-time buckets, likes, shares): explicit stars are sparse and biased since most users never rate, while implicit signals are abundant but carry their own biases—label construction is itself a design choice.
tradeoff: 隐式反馈(量大全覆盖但有偏) vs 显式打星(直接但稀疏有偏)
options: 用显式打星，因为它最直接反映用户的真实评价
用隐式反馈(观看时长分桶、点赞、转发)构造标签
随机采样一批视频请人工标注，完全忽略用户行为
只用视频元数据(时长、分辨率、标签)推断相关性
options_en: Use explicit stars, since they most directly reflect the user’s true evaluation.
Build labels from implicit feedback: watch-time buckets, likes, and shares.
Randomly sample videos for human annotation, ignoring user behavior entirely.
Infer relevance only from video metadata: duration, resolution, and tags.
whenOtherWins: 若产品本身有强显式评分文化(如电影评分站、明确 1-5 星)且样本充足，显式标签更干净、可直接当 ground truth。
optionExplanations: 显式打星虽直接但极稀疏、只有少数活跃用户打，样本量撑不起训练。
对；隐式反馈量大覆盖全，是主流做法；但要意识到它带偏差，标签构造是设计决策。
人工标注不可扩展、且脱离真实用户偏好，不适合数百万视频规模。
元数据不反映相关性——分辨率高不等于用户想看，信号错位。
optionExplanations_en: Explicit stars are direct but extremely sparse—only a few active users rate—so the sample size cannot support training.
Correct — implicit feedback is abundant and full-coverage, the mainstream approach; but recognize its bias, and label construction is a design choice.
Human annotation does not scale and detaches from real user preference, unfit for millions of videos.
Metadata does not reflect relevance—high resolution does not mean the user wants it, a mismatched signal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从用户行为(观看时长、点赞、转发)间接推断偏好，无需用户主动评分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Implicit feedback infers preference from behavior (watch time, likes, shares) without users actively rating.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被当作正确答案的参考标签，这里由隐式反馈构造。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Ground truth is the reference label treated as correct, here built from implicit feedback.

scenario: 团队只跑离线指标(Recall@K、NDCG@K)就想直接上线新模型。
scenario_en: The team wants to ship a new model based on offline metrics (Recall@K, NDCG@K) alone.
q: 为什么离线指标是「必要但不充分」，必须再做在线评估？
q_en: Why are offline metrics 'necessary but not sufficient', requiring online evaluation?
why: 离线指标只衡量与历史行为的相关性，抓不住新颖性、多样性、长期满意度。历史标签里没有的行为(如用户对全新内容的反应)离线看不到，必须靠在线 A/B 才能测真实因果影响。
why_en: Offline metrics only measure correlation with historical behavior and miss novelty, diversity, and long-term satisfaction, so real causal impact must be tested with online A/B.
options: 离线指标只反映历史行为相关性，抓不住新颖性
离线指标已经覆盖一切，在线 A/B 只是浪费流量和迭代时间
在线评估只是为了测服务延迟，和推荐质量无关
离线指标完全不可信，应彻底弃用，只看在线结果
options_en: Offline metrics only reflect correlation with historical behavior and miss novelty.
Offline metrics already cover everything, so online A/B just wastes traffic and iteration time.
Online evaluation only measures serving latency and is unrelated to recommendation quality.
Offline metrics are wholly untrustworthy and should be dropped for online results only.
optionExplanations: 对；离线是历史相关性，抓不到新颖/多样/长期满意这些只有真实上线才暴露的维度。
离线看不到用户对全新内容的反应，也测不了长期满意，覆盖不了一切。
在线评估的核心是真实用户行为的因果影响，不只是延迟。
离线便宜、能快速筛掉坏模型，是必要的第一道关，不该弃用。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — offline is historical correlation and misses novelty/diversity/long-term satisfaction, dimensions only real deployment exposes.
Offline cannot see how users react to brand-new content nor measure long-term satisfaction, so it does not cover everything.
Online evaluation is about causal impact on real user behavior, not just latency.
Offline is cheap and quickly filters bad models, a necessary first gate, not to be discarded.

termDefinitions.meaning: 推荐内容对用户的新鲜程度，离线历史标签无法衡量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Novelty is how fresh recommended content is to the user, which offline historical labels cannot measure.

scenario: 新排序模型通过了离线评估，要在真实流量上验证，但不想拿全量用户冒险。
scenario_en: A new ranker passed offline evaluation and needs live validation, but you don't want to risk all users.
q: A/B 测试初期该怎么设置对照/实验组和流量比例？
q_en: How should you set up control/treatment and traffic split for an early A/B?
why: 对照组看现网模型、实验组看候选模型，随机分流，初期只放 1–5% 小流量灰度。小比例把风险控制住，出问题只影响少数用户，指标稳了再逐步放量。
why_en: Control sees the production model, treatment sees the candidate, split randomly, ramping only 1–5% initially so a bad model hits few users before scaling up.
tradeoff: 小流量灰度(风险可控但样本慢) vs 大流量(统计快但风险大)
options: 直接全量切到新模型，最快拿到统计显著的结果
对照和实验各占 50%，一上来就对半分全部流量
只在内部员工账号上灰度，不放任何真实用户
对照看现网、实验看候选，初期只放 1–5% 流量
options_en: Switch all traffic to the new model at once for the fastest significant result.
Split control and treatment 50/50, halving all traffic from day one.
Roll out only to internal employee accounts, exposing no real users.
Control sees production, treatment sees the candidate, ramping at only 1–5% at first.
whenOtherWins: 若改动极小、风险低且需要尽快达到统计功效(如微小 UI 文案)，可直接用较大比例甚至对半分加速实验。
optionExplanations: 全量切换一旦模型坏了会伤害所有用户，风险太大，违背灰度原则。
初期就对半分暴露过多用户，坏模型影响面太大；应先小流量确认安全。
只测员工样本无代表性、样本量小，测不出真实用户的行为差异。
对；小流量灰度是标准做法——先小规模验证安全和信号，再逐步放量。
optionExplanations_en: Full switch harms all users if the model is bad—too risky, against ramp-up principle.
A 50/50 split up front exposes too many users; confirm safety at small traffic first.
Employee-only samples are unrepresentative and too small to detect real user differences.
Correct — small-traffic ramp is standard: validate safety and signal at small scale, then scale up.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对照组用现网模型、实验组用候选模型，随机分流后比较指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Control uses the production model and treatment the candidate; users are split randomly and metrics compared.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从小流量比例开始逐步扩大实验组，控制风险。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ramp gradually grows the treatment traffic from a small percentage to control risk.

scenario: A/B 里既有想拉高的指标，也有绝不能恶化的红线指标。
scenario_en: An A/B has both metrics to lift and red-line metrics that must never regress.
q: 在线 A/B 的 primary metric 和 guardrail metric 有什么区别？
q_en: What distinguishes a primary metric from a guardrail metric in online A/B?
why: Primary(观看时长/session、满意度代理)是主动优化目标；guardrail(不喜欢率、举报、退订、session 放弃)不直接优化，但不能越过阈值恶化——越线就叫停实验，无论参与度涨多少。
why_en: Primary metrics (watch time/session, satisfaction proxies) are actively optimized; guardrail metrics (dislike, report, unsubscribe, abandonment) are not optimized but must not regress past a threshold—breach kills the experiment regardless of engagement gains.
tradeoff: primary(要拉高) vs guardrail(只守不恶化，越线即叫停)
options: primary 和 guardrail 都是要最大化的目标，只是优先级不同
primary 是主动优化的目标；guardrail 越阈值即叫停
guardrail 是主动优化目标，primary 只是背景监控
两者都只在离线评估阶段使用，在线 A/B 里完全不看
options_en: Both primary and guardrail are metrics to maximize, differing only in priority.
Primary is the metric you actively optimize; a guardrail breach kills the experiment.
Guardrail is the actively optimized metric and primary is just background monitoring.
Both are used only during offline evaluation and never looked at in online A/B.
optionExplanations: guardrail 不是要最大化的，而是「不能变坏」的红线，二者角色不同。
对；primary 拉高、guardrail 守底线，guardrail 越线即杀实验是硬安全网。
说反了：guardrail 只守不优化，primary 才是主动拉高的目标。
两者都是在线 A/B 的核心指标，恰恰是上线前的真实检验。
optionExplanations_en: Guardrails are not to be maximized but are a red line that 'must not worsen'; the roles differ.
Correct — primary rises, guardrail holds the floor, and a guardrail breach kills the experiment as a hard safety net.
Backwards: guardrails only hold and are not optimized; primary is the metric actively lifted.
Both are core online A/B metrics, exactly the real pre-launch test.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不被直接优化但不能恶化的红线指标(不喜欢率、退订、放弃率)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A guardrail metric is a red-line metric that is not optimized directly but must not regress (dislike, unsubscribe, abandonment).

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户在一次会话中提前离开的比例，是护栏指标之一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Session abandonment is the rate at which users leave a session early, one guardrail metric.

scenario: A/B 结果：观看时长 +3%，但不喜欢率 +15%、7 天回访 −2%(护栏指标越过阈值)。
scenario_en: A/B result: watch time +3%, but dislike rate +15% and 7-day return −2% (guardrails past threshold).
q: 这个实验该怎么处理？
q_en: How should this experiment be handled?
why: 护栏(不喜欢、7 天回访)已越阈值恶化，无论观看时长涨多少都该叫停。+3% 参与度换 +15% 不喜欢、−2% 回访是净亏，护栏就是拦这种「短期涨、长期崩」的安全网。
why_en: Guardrails (dislike, 7-day return) regressed past threshold, so kill the experiment regardless of the +3% watch time—it is a net loss and guardrails exist to block short-term-up long-term-down trades.
tradeoff: 护栏越线即叫停(护长期) vs 只看主指标上线(赚短期赔长期)
options: 上线：观看时长涨了 +3%，主指标为正就够了
把不喜欢率的阈值调宽，让实验通过评审后再上线
叫停实验：护栏越阈值恶化，参与度增益抵不过
延长实验到 3 个月，等护栏指标自己回落
options_en: Ship it: watch time rose +3%, a positive primary metric is enough.
Widen the dislike-rate threshold so the experiment passes review, then ship.
Kill it: the guardrails regressed past threshold and the engagement gain does not offset that.
Extend the experiment to 3 months and wait for guardrails to recover on their own.
whenOtherWins: 若护栏波动只是新鲜效应导致的短期噪声、且在 1–2 周内回到阈值内，可继续观察而非立即杀掉。
optionExplanations: 只看主指标会放任 cannibalization：+3% 观看时长换来 +15% 不喜欢和回访下降，得不偿失。
为通过而放宽护栏是自欺欺人，护栏的意义正是拦住这种交易。
对；护栏越线即杀是硬安全网，短期参与度增益盖不住长期满意度崩塌。
拖 3 个月既伤害用户又浪费流量，护栏恶化不会因为等待而自愈。
optionExplanations_en: Looking at the primary metric alone lets cannibalization run: +3% watch time for +15% dislike and lower return is a bad trade.
Widening guardrails to pass is self-deception; guardrails exist precisely to block this trade.
Correct — breach-kill is a hard safety net; short-term engagement gains cannot cover long-term satisfaction collapse.
Dragging on 3 months harms users and wastes traffic; a guardrail regression will not self-heal by waiting.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户在 7 天内再次回来的比例，是长期满意度的护栏代理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: 7-day return rate is the share of users who come back within 7 days, a guardrail proxy for long-term satisfaction.

scenario: 有人想把 A/B 只跑 2 天就下结论，因为实验组观看时长立刻大涨。
scenario_en: Someone wants to conclude an A/B after just 2 days because treatment watch time jumped immediately.
q: A/B 一般要跑多久，为什么不能只跑两天？
q_en: How long should an A/B usually run, and why not just two days?
why: 典型跑 1–2 周(经验值，非公式)来吸收新颖效应——用户对任何新东西头几天都更爱互动，过早下结论会把这段虚高当成真实收益，得到误导性的「假赢」。
why_en: Run 1–2 weeks (a rule of thumb, not a formula) to absorb novelty effects—users engage more with anything new in the first days, so cutting short mistakes that spike for real gains, a misleading false win.
options: 典型 1–2 周，用来吸收新颖效应，避免把头几天的虚高当真实收益
只需几小时，指标一出现好转波动就能立刻下结论，不必等待
至少要跑一整年，运行时间短于一年的实验结果都不可信
必须跑到样本量正好凑够 100 条为止，和运行了多久完全无关
options_en: Typically 1–2 weeks, to absorb novelty effects and avoid mistaking a first-days spike for real gains.
Just a few hours — once the metric shows any positive blip you can conclude immediately, no need to wait.
At least a full year is required; any experiment run for less than a year is untrustworthy.
Must run until the sample size hits exactly 100, entirely independent of how long it ran.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户对任何新东西头几天都更爱互动的短期现象，会虚高实验指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The novelty effect is users engaging more with anything new in its first days, transiently inflating experiment metrics.

optionExplanations: 对，这是常见经验做法——留出十来天时间，让用户对新鲜事物的短暂热情自然褪去，再看数据是否真的站得住。
错，几小时连新鲜感尖峰都还没退，此时看到的正向数字大概率只是噪声或凑巧的短期波动。
错，一整年既拖慢迭代节奏，又让业务变化和季节因素混进来，反而让对比失真。
错，样本量当然要看，但只认一个固定数字、不管时间窗口，照样会被新鲜效应带偏。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — running about ten days to two weeks lets the initial novelty spike fade before you trust the numbers.
Wrong — a few hours isn't enough for the novelty spike to fade, so an early positive reading is likely just noise.
Wrong — a full year both stalls iteration and lets seasonal shifts creep in, distorting the comparison.
Wrong — a fixed sample size ignoring the time window still lets novelty bias skew the result.

scenario: 早期迭代流量有限，想更快、用更小样本比较两个排序模型的相对优劣。
scenario_en: Early iterations have limited traffic, and you want a faster, smaller-sample comparison of two rankers.
q: 流量有限的早期迭代，interleaving 相比标准 A/B 有什么优势？
q_en: For early iterations with limited traffic, what advantage does interleaving have over standard A/B?
why: Interleaving 把对照和实验的排序在同一次会话里交错混排，让同一用户直接比较两者，控制了用户异质性，所以用更小样本就能得出偏好，适合流量有限的早期迭代。
why_en: Interleaving mixes control and treatment rankings within one session so the same user directly compares both, controlling user heterogeneity and needing smaller samples—good for early low-traffic iterations.
tradeoff: interleaving(同人对比·省样本·比相对偏好) vs A/B(分人对比·需大样本·测绝对指标)
options: interleaving 能测长期留存这种绝对指标，A/B 不能
把两模型排序在同一会话交错混排，同一用户直接比较
interleaving 不需要现网模型做对照，直接单独跑候选
interleaving 完全取代 A/B，任何阶段都优于分组实验
options_en: Interleaving can measure absolute metrics like long-term retention, which A/B cannot.
Mix both models’ rankings within one session so the same user compares them directly.
Interleaving needs no production model as control and just runs the candidate alone.
Interleaving fully replaces A/B and beats split experiments at every stage.
whenOtherWins: 若要测长期留存、收入这类绝对业务指标或需要护栏监控，标准 A/B 更合适——interleaving 只给相对排序偏好。
optionExplanations: 反了：绝对指标(长期留存)是 A/B 的强项，interleaving 给的是相对偏好。
对；同一用户内对比消除了个体差异，统计功效高，小样本即可比出谁更好。
它恰恰要把现网和候选两个排序混在一起比，缺了对照就无从比较。
它给不出绝对业务指标和护栏读数，替代不了分组实验。
optionExplanations_en: Reversed: absolute metrics (long-term retention) are A/B's strength; interleaving gives relative preference.
Correct — within-user comparison removes individual variance, giving high power so a small sample settles which is better.
It specifically mixes the production and candidate rankings together, so it still needs the control source.
It cannot produce absolute business metrics or guardrail readings, so it does not replace split experiments.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把两个模型的排序在同一会话交错混排，让同一用户直接比较，样本效率高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Interleaving mixes two models' rankings within one session so the same user compares both, giving high sample efficiency.

scenario: 端到端延迟预算是 <200ms，要分配给候选生成、排序、重排三段。
scenario_en: The end-to-end budget is <200ms, split across candidate generation, ranking, and re-ranking.
q: <200ms 是怎样的预算，各阶段大致怎么分，对模型有什么约束？
q_en: What kind of budget is <200ms, how is it split, and what does it constrain?
why: <200ms 是给定的产品/SLO 目标(不是公式推出来的)。核心分配约候选生成 ~20ms + 排序 ~50ms + 重排 ~10ms，其余留给网络和特征拉取。它直接约束排序模型大小——大到跑不进预算就得压缩。
why_en: The <200ms is a given product/SLO target (not derived), split roughly ~20ms candidate gen + ~50ms ranking + ~10ms re-rank with the rest for network/features, and it directly caps the ranker's size.
options: 候选生成~20ms+排序~50ms+重排~10ms，其余留给网络特征，直接约束模型大小
这是训练阶段允许的时长上限，跟线上请求的响应延迟完全无关
把全部 200ms 时间都只分给排序阶段，召回和重排两个环节完全不占用时间
它衡量的是模型准确率必须达到的下限指标，不是对响应延迟的约束
options_en: ~20ms candidate gen + ~50ms ranking + ~10ms re-rank, rest for network/features — it directly caps the ranker's size.
This is a training-time duration ceiling, unrelated to the online request's response latency.
All 200ms goes only to the ranking stage; retrieval and re-ranking take up no time at all.
It measures the minimum accuracy threshold the model must hit, not a constraint on response latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 端到端允许的最大响应时间，超了会增加会话放弃，是给定 SLO 而非算出来的。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A latency budget is the max end-to-end response time allowed; exceeding it raises abandonment, and it is a given SLO rather than a computed value.

optionExplanations: 对，这套~20/50/10ms 的分配把重计算限制在预算内，模型大小和推理速度也因此被这条硬线卡死。
错，训练时长你想跑多久都行，跟在线一次请求要多快返回完全是两回事。
错，全部时间只给排序，召回和重排就没法运作，漏斗式流水线也就散架了。
错，这是响应速度的硬性上限，不是拿来衡量模型准不准的门槛。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — that ~20/50/10ms split keeps the heavy compute inside budget, and it's exactly what caps how big and slow the ranker is allowed to be.
Wrong — training can take as long as you like; that's unrelated to how fast one online request must return.
Wrong — giving all the time to ranking leaves nothing for retrieval or re-ranking, so the funnel pipeline falls apart.
Wrong — this is a hard ceiling on response speed, not a bar for how accurate the model has to be.

scenario: 候选生成要在 ~20ms 内从数百万视频里选出 ~500 个候选。
scenario_en: Candidate generation must select ~500 candidates from millions of videos within ~20ms.
q: 候选生成为什么能在 ~20ms 内跑完，在线主要花在哪？
q_en: How does candidate generation finish in ~20ms, and where does its online cost go?
why: 视频 embedding 离线预计算好、建成索引，在线只需把用户上下文编码成 query embedding，再用 ANN 查最近邻。在线成本 = 一次 query 编码 + 一次索引查找，所以能压到 ~20ms，优先保召回和吞吐。
why_en: Video embeddings are precomputed offline into an index, so online cost is just encoding the user context into a query embedding plus one ANN lookup, keeping it near ~20ms while prioritizing recall and throughput.
tradeoff: 视频侧离线预计算(在线只查) vs 在线实时算视频 embedding(准但太慢)
options: 在线对每个视频实时重算 embedding，再逐个和用户比对
视频 embedding 离线预计算成索引，在线只做 ANN 查找
把数百万视频全量灌进排序模型逐个实时打分
在数据库里用 SQL 关键词匹配视频标题挑候选
options_en: Recompute each video's embedding online in real time and compare with the user one by one.
Video embeddings are precomputed offline into an index; online does only an ANN lookup.
Feed all millions of videos into the ranking model and score them one by one in real time.
Pick candidates by SQL keyword matching on video titles in the database.
whenOtherWins: 若物料库极小或视频特征高频变化到无法预计算，才考虑在线实时算 embedding；一般规模下预计算+ANN 才跑得进预算。
optionExplanations: 在线实时算数百万 embedding 远超 20ms，正是预计算要避免的。
对；预计算把重活挪到离线，在线只剩编码+查找，才压得进 ~20ms。
全量灌排序模型是数百万次重推理，秒级都不止，违背两阶段设计。
关键词匹配抓不到语义相似，召回质量差，也不是 embedding 检索。
optionExplanations_en: Computing millions of embeddings online far exceeds 20ms—exactly what precomputation avoids.
Correct — precomputation moves the heavy work offline, leaving only encode plus lookup online to fit ~20ms.
Feeding all into the ranker is millions of heavy inferences, seconds not ms, violating the two-stage design.
Keyword matching misses semantic similarity, giving poor recall, and is not embedding retrieval.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户上下文编码成的向量，用它在视频索引里做 ANN 最近邻查找。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A query embedding encodes the user context into a vector used for ANN nearest-neighbor lookup in the video index.

scenario: 排序阶段的 Wide&Deep/DCN 模型要在 ~50ms 内给几百候选打分，模型大小被延迟卡住。
scenario_en: The ranking-stage Wide&Deep/DCN must score hundreds of candidates within ~50ms, its size capped by latency.
q: 哪些技术能让排序模型在延迟预算内跑得动？(多选)
q_en: Which techniques help the ranking model fit within the latency budget? (multiple)
why: 压延迟的三招：模型蒸馏(小学生模型模仿大老师)、量化(FP32→INT8 减算力)、embedding table distribution(把稀疏 embedding 表分片到多机并行查)。加大 batch 上限不是降延迟手段。
why_en: Three levers: model distillation (small student mimics big teacher), quantization (FP32→INT8), and embedding-table distribution (shard sparse tables across machines for parallel lookup); raising the batch cap is not a latency reducer.
options: 模型蒸馏：小学生模型模仿大老师，参数更少推理更快
量化：把权重从 FP32 降到 INT8，减少算力和内存
embedding table distribution：把稀疏 embedding 表分片到多机，并行查找
把推理 batch 上限调大，让单次处理更多请求
options_en: Model distillation: a small student mimics a big teacher, fewer params and faster inference.
Quantization: drop weights from FP32 to INT8, cutting compute and memory.
Embedding-table distribution: shard sparse embedding tables across machines for parallel lookup.
Raise the inference batch cap so one pass handles more requests.
optionExplanations: 对；蒸馏用小模型逼近大模型精度，直接砍推理成本，是压延迟主力。
对；INT8 让每次乘加更快、内存更省，是常见的推理加速手段。
对；YouTube 规模稀疏表装不下单机，分片并行查是必需，也带来分布式推理的容错课题。
错；加大 batch 提高吞吐但通常增加单请求延迟(等凑批)，不是降延迟。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — distillation approximates the big model's accuracy with a small one, directly cutting inference cost, a primary latency lever.
Correct — INT8 makes each multiply-add faster and saves memory, a common inference speedup.
Correct — at YouTube scale sparse tables cannot fit one machine, so sharded parallel lookup is required, introducing distributed-inference fault-tolerance concerns.
Wrong — a larger batch raises throughput but usually increases per-request latency (waiting to fill the batch), not reduces it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把模型权重从高精度(FP32)降到低精度(INT8)，减少算力和内存、略损精度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Quantization lowers model weights from high precision (FP32) to low (INT8), cutting compute and memory with slight accuracy loss.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练一个小的学生模型去模仿大的老师模型输出，换取更快推理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Model distillation trains a small student model to mimic a large teacher's outputs for faster inference.

scenario: YouTube 规模的稀疏特征 embedding 表(数亿 ID)大到一台机器的内存装不下。
scenario_en: At YouTube scale, sparse-feature embedding tables (hundreds of millions of IDs) are too big for one machine's memory.
q: 稀疏 embedding 表装不下单机时，怎么在服务里处理？代价是什么？
q_en: When sparse embedding tables don't fit one machine, how is this handled at serving, and at what cost?
why: 把 embedding 表分片(shard)到多台机器，推理时并行查各分片再汇总(分布式推理)。代价：跨机通信增加延迟，且引入容错问题——某个分片机器挂了要有降级/副本，否则查不到那部分特征。
why_en: Shard the embedding table across machines and do parallel lookups gathered at inference (distributed inference); the cost is added cross-machine latency plus fault-tolerance concerns if a shard host fails.
tradeoff: 分片分布式推理(装得下大表但加通信+容错) vs 单机(简单但装不下)
options: 把 embedding 表分片到多机并行查找；代价是跨机延迟
把稀疏 ID 全哈希进一个小表，接受大量冲突以塞进单机
干脆不用稀疏特征，只保留稠密特征以缩小模型体积
把整张表完整复制到每台机器上，靠冗余提速
options_en: Shard the embedding table across machines with parallel lookups; the cost is cross-machine latency.
Hash all sparse IDs into one small table, accepting heavy collisions to fit one machine.
Drop sparse features entirely and keep only dense ones to shrink the model.
Replicate the entire table onto every machine and rely on redundancy for speed.
whenOtherWins: 若稀疏表小到能装进单机内存，就别上分布式——单机查找没有跨机通信和分片容错开销，更简单更快。
optionExplanations: 对；分片+分布式推理是装下大表的标准解，代价是通信延迟和分片容错，Staff+ 要点名。
全哈希进小表冲突严重、信息大量丢失，损精度换空间不是这里的正解。
丢掉稀疏特征会损失关键个性化信号，是削足适履。
整表复制到每机内存翻倍更装不下，也不解决单机放不下的根本问题。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — sharding plus distributed inference is the standard way to fit a large table; the cost is communication latency and shard fault tolerance, a Staff+ point.
Hashing everything into a small table causes heavy collisions and information loss, trading accuracy for space, not the fix here.
Dropping sparse features loses key personalization signal, cutting the foot to fit the shoe.
Replicating the whole table onto every machine doubles memory and still cannot fit, not solving the root problem.

termDefinitions.term: embedding table distribution / embedding 表分布
termDefinitions.meaning: 把巨大的稀疏 embedding 表分片到多台机器，推理时并行查找。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Embedding-table distribution shards a huge sparse embedding table across machines for parallel lookup at inference.

termDefinitions.meaning: 推理跨多台机器协同完成，带来通信延迟和容错需求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Distributed inference splits one inference across machines, adding communication latency and fault-tolerance needs.

scenario: 团队一路加大观看时长权重，指标持续上涨，但用户自报满意度悄悄下滑。
scenario_en: The team keeps raising the watch-time weight and the metric keeps climbing, but self-reported satisfaction quietly slips.
q: 指标相食(metric cannibalization)最典型的一对是什么，本质是什么问题？
q_en: What is the canonical cannibalization pair, and what kind of problem is it fundamentally?
why: 最典型是观看时长 vs 长期满意度：最大化观看时长会顶起自动播放友好的煽动内容，人一直看却不满意；YouTube 自己的研究证实纯参与度优化拉低了自报满意度。它没有银弹，是需要持续校准的问题，不是一次性可解。
why_en: The canonical pair is watch time vs long-term satisfaction: maximizing watch time surfaces autoplay-friendly sensational content that keeps users watching yet dissatisfied, a continuous calibration problem with no silver bullet.
options: 延迟 vs 吞吐：压低延迟必然降吞吐，属硬件权衡
召回 vs 精度：多召回必然掉精度，靠调 K 解决
观看时长 vs 长期满意度：优化时长会顶起煽动内容
训练成本 vs 推理成本：省训练必然贵推理
options_en: Latency vs throughput: cutting latency must lower throughput, a hardware tradeoff.
Recall vs precision: more recall must drop precision, fixed by tuning K.
Watch time vs long-term satisfaction: optimizing time surfaces sensational content.
Training cost vs inference cost: saving training must raise inference.
optionExplanations: 延迟-吞吐是资源权衡，不是「优化一个业务指标拖垮另一个业务指标」的相食。
召回-精度是检索权衡，不涉及长期满意度被短期参与度侵蚀。
对；观看时长顶起煽动内容侵蚀长期满意，是相食的教科书案例，需持续校准。
训练-推理成本是工程成本权衡，不是指标相食。
optionExplanations_en: Latency-throughput is a resource tradeoff, not one business metric systematically degrading another.
Recall-precision is a retrieval tradeoff and does not involve long-term satisfaction eroded by short-term engagement.
Correct — watch time surfacing sensational content that erodes long-term satisfaction is the textbook cannibalization case, needing continuous calibration.
Training-inference cost is an engineering-cost tradeoff, not metric cannibalization.

termDefinitions.meaning: 优化一个指标系统性地拖垮另一个，如观看时长涨但长期满意度掉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Metric cannibalization is when optimizing one metric systematically degrades another, e.g. watch time up but long-term satisfaction down.

scenario: 已知观看时长在蚕食长期满意度，要在建模和部署层面缓解。
scenario_en: Given that watch time is cannibalizing long-term satisfaction, you need modeling and deployment-level mitigations.
q: 缓解指标相食有哪些正当手段？(多选)
q_en: Which are legitimate ways to mitigate metric cannibalization? (multiple)
why: 四类缓解里的三类：多目标标量化(加满意度头、按 surface 调权)、长视野奖励建模(预测 N 天回访、用 RL 处理延迟奖励)、护栏门控部署(满意度护栏恶化就不上线)。「删掉满意度指标」是掩耳盗铃，不是缓解。
why_en: Three legitimate levers: multi-objective scalarization (satisfaction heads, per-surface weights), long-horizon reward modeling (predicted N-day return, RL for delayed rewards), and guardrail-gated deployment; deleting the satisfaction metric is not a mitigation.
options: 多目标标量化：加满意度预测头、按 surface 调权
长视野奖励建模：预测 N 天回访率，用 RL 处理延迟奖励
护栏门控部署：满意度护栏(不喜欢、放弃率)恶化就不上线
干脆不再统计满意度指标，眼不见为净
options_en: Multi-objective scalarization: add satisfaction heads and tune weights per surface.
Long-horizon reward modeling: predict N-day return rate and use RL for delayed rewards.
Guardrail-gated deployment: do not ship if satisfaction guardrails (dislike, abandonment) regress.
Just stop tracking the satisfaction metric to keep it out of sight.
optionExplanations: 对；标量化加满意度头把长期满意变成可优化信号，是最直接的缓解。
对；长视野奖励把 N 天回访纳入目标，缓解只看即时观看时长的短视。
对；护栏门控是硬安全网，满意度恶化直接拦下上线。
错；停统计不解决问题，只是让相食无人察觉，是反面做法。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — scalarization with satisfaction heads turns long-term satisfaction into an optimizable signal, the most direct mitigation.
Correct — long-horizon rewards fold N-day return into the objective, easing the short-sightedness of raw watch time.
Correct — guardrail gating is a hard safety net that blocks shipping when satisfaction regresses.
Wrong — not tracking it solves nothing and just lets cannibalization go unnoticed, an anti-pattern.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 N 天回访等延迟结果纳入优化目标，对抗只看即时观看的短视。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A long-horizon reward folds delayed outcomes like N-day return into the objective to counter short-term myopia.

scenario: 一部分用户出现明显不满信号(打开频率下降、不喜欢上升)，另一部分仍很活跃满意。
scenario_en: Some users show clear dissatisfaction (declining frequency, rising dislikes) while others remain active and satisfied.
q: 怎么用「按用户分群调权」缓解这部分用户的相食？
q_en: How does per-user-segment weight tuning mitigate cannibalization for these users?
why: 排序分 = w_满意度×满意度预测 + w_时长×观看时长预测；对不满分群调高 w_满意度、压低 w_时长，其余分群维持原权重。
why_en: The ranking score is w_sat × predicted satisfaction + w_time × predicted watch time; for the dissatisfied segment you raise w_sat and cut w_time, leaving other segments unchanged.
tradeoff: 按分群调权(精准但更复杂) vs 全局一套权重(简单但对不满用户失灵)
options: 对不满分群提高满意度权重、降低观看时长权重
对所有用户统一把观看时长权重再调高，摊平差异
把不满用户直接从推荐系统里剔除，不再服务
只按用户地理位置分群，与满意信号无关
options_en: For the dissatisfied segment, raise the satisfaction weight and lower the watch-time weight.
Uniformly raise the watch-time weight for every user to flatten the differences.
Remove dissatisfied users from the system entirely and stop serving them.
Segment only by geography, unrelated to the satisfaction signal.
whenOtherWins: 若各分群的不满模式差别不大、或分群带来的复杂度/数据稀疏得不偿失，一套全局权重反而更稳更好维护。
optionExplanations: 对；对不满分群定向加满意度权重，是把校准做到人群粒度，正对相食。
全局再调高观看时长权重会让不满用户更糟，方向反了。
剔除用户是放弃而非缓解，还会流失用户，不是调权手段。
只按地理分群抓不到「谁在不满」，与缓解相食的目标脱节。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — targeting the dissatisfied segment with a higher satisfaction weight brings calibration down to the segment level, directly addressing cannibalization.
Raising the watch-time weight globally makes dissatisfied users worse—the wrong direction.
Removing users is giving up, not mitigating, and churns users, not a weighting lever.
Segmenting by geography alone cannot capture who is dissatisfied, detached from the mitigation goal.

termDefinitions.term: per-segment weight tuning / 分群调权
termDefinitions.meaning: 对不同用户分群使用不同的目标权重，对不满群体加大满意度权重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Per-segment weight tuning uses different objective weights for different user segments, boosting satisfaction weight for dissatisfied groups.

scenario: 一次在线请求进来，要在 <200ms 内走完两阶段服务并返回一屏推荐。
scenario_en: One online request arrives and must traverse two-stage serving within <200ms to return a screen.
q: 把在线服务一次请求的处理步骤排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the steps of serving one online request correctly:
steps: 把用户上下文编码成 query embedding
用 ANN 查预计算的视频索引，召回 ~500 候选
排序模型对候选算多目标分并排序
重排注入多样性并施加硬性政策过滤，返回一屏
why: 顺序：编码 query→ANN 召回~500→排序精算打分→重排(多样性+硬过滤)出屏。前两步是候选生成(~20ms)、第三步排序(~50ms)、第四步重排(~10ms)，合计核心~80ms 落进 <200ms。
why_en: Order: encode query, ANN-retrieve ~500, rank with multi-objective scores, then re-rank (diversity + hard filters), i.e. ~20ms + ~50ms + ~10ms of core compute inside <200ms.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  E["编码 query embedding"] --> A["ANN 召回 ~500"]
  A --> R["排序多目标打分"]
  R --> RR["重排+硬过滤→出屏"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 候选生成(召回)+排序(精排)的在线漏斗，末端加重排，整体受延迟预算约束。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-stage serving is the online funnel of candidate generation (retrieval) plus ranking, with re-ranking at the end, all under a latency budget.

scenario: 同一道视频推荐题，L4、L5、Staff+ 候选人的答法差在哪。
scenario_en: For the same video-rec question, how do L4, L5, and Staff+ answers differ.
q: 区分 Staff+ 与更初级答案的核心是什么？
q_en: What core thing separates a Staff+ answer from more junior ones?
why: Staff+ 的差异不是「知道更多事实」，而是能跨整个生命周期(训练→服务→评估→迭代)做取舍推理：把系统框成持续校准回路，讲相食缓解、embedding 表分布、评估里的公平监控。L4 只认出两阶段+基本指标。
why_en: The Staff+ differentiator is not knowing more facts but reasoning about trade-offs across the whole lifecycle (training, serving, evaluation, iteration) and framing the system as a continuous calibration loop.
tradeoff: Staff+ 全生命周期取舍推理 vs L4 罗列组件与指标
options: 背下更多算法名词、论文和公式推导细节
能跨训练/服务/评估/迭代做全生命周期取舍推理
把两阶段流水线和 NDCG/Recall 名字说全就够
画出最复杂的架构图，组件画得越多越好
options_en: Memorizing more algorithm names, papers, and formula derivations.
Reasoning about trade-offs across the whole training, serving, evaluation, and iteration lifecycle.
Just naming the two-stage pipeline and NDCG/Recall.
Drawing the most complex architecture diagram, with as many boxes as possible.
optionExplanations: 多背名词是知识堆砌，Staff+ 看的是判断和取舍，不是词汇量。
对；全生命周期的取舍推理 + 持续校准框架，才是 Staff+ 的分水岭。
认出两阶段和基本指标是 L4 层次，还谈不上取舍深度。
组件堆得多不等于想得深，复杂度不是信号，取舍才是。
optionExplanations_en: Memorizing terms is knowledge stacking; Staff+ is judged on judgment and trade-offs, not vocabulary.
Correct — full-lifecycle trade-off reasoning plus a continuous-calibration framing is the Staff+ divide.
Naming the two stages and basic metrics is the L4 level, not yet trade-off depth.
More components is not deeper thinking; complexity is not the signal, trade-offs are.

termDefinitions.term: continuous calibration loop / 持续校准回路
termDefinitions.meaning: 把推荐系统当作永远在调、never done 的反馈优化过程，而非一次性交付。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A continuous calibration loop treats the recommender as never-done, always being retuned rather than a one-off delivery.
